cross_cutting_mbo_finding: The g19 EIA-day tape reads the crowded-short unwind directly, and the covering is a SIZE-WEIGHTED flow event invisible to count-based bid share. 05-14 D-1 tape (05-13) is coherent sell-lean - signed_flow -2763, phases [9,-1979,-793] (selling accelerating), session_b 0.444 ~= big_print_b 0.458 (both <0.5, agree) - shorts still pressing into the first print. 05-21 D-1 tape (05-20) FLIPS to accelerating aggressive BUY - signed_flow +1892, phases [-225,+614,+1503] (buy building into the print) - yet count-based session_b stays sell-lean at 0.425 (big_print_b 0.476). That divergence (few large lifters vs many small sellers) is the covering signature: the short-covering shows in size-weighted signed flow while count-share still reads sell. Because both prints are in-line/telegraphed and the recent builds run tighter than the 5yr norm (chg_vs_5yr_chg -19.8), the print delivers no surprise fuel - so the in-line 05-14 caps the short press (absorption, damped down) and the 05-21 covering delivers up, with the larger-injection print + over-extension damping it two-sided. General mechanism: on a crowded-short block, an in-line EIA print sorts by delivery/absorption, and the covering bid is a size-weighted lift the count-based b_share misses (+n).
